messages:
opsbot: :rotating_light: Alert: KV cache churn spike detected in us-west-2 cluster. continuous-batching throughput decreased, block_manager evictions rising. 95p tail latency +120ms, error rate +0.8% over last 3m. alert link: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/1945679012

maria: paging in — oncall? seeing big metadata growth on paged-kv, looks like small blocks are being created rapidly (block_count +85% in 5m). potential leak in block reference accounting.

ashok: i'm oncall, joining. can you share which services are hit and any customer-facing errors?

jamie: scope: inference-runtime (hosted) and dedicated pools in us-west-2. customer-facing: a handful of low-volume enterprise tenants report increased response time and a small number of transient 500s on generate endpoints. Not universal.

sofia: quick metric dump: kv_block_count: 1.9M -> 3.5M, avg_block_size: 2.1KB -> 1.2KB, eviction_ops/sec: 18 -> 140, continuous_batch_window_ms: 40 -> 120 (auto-bump).

ashok: suspected cause: continuous-batching heuristics are growing batch length under load, pushing more KV allocations and causing block fragmentation. If eviction thrash hits the block manager we see perf cliffs. mitigation idea 1: reduce continuous_batch_window to 30ms for us-west-2. mitigation idea 2: increase min_block_size to avoid tiny block allocations.

maria: agree. we should also temporarily disable prefix caching for high-cardinality keys (prompt-hashes) to reduce duplication in the KV layer.

jamie: can we apply a hot runtime flag? we have a runtime config that supports per-region overrides. propose immediate actions: 1) set continuous_batch_window_ms=30 via /runtime-config API, 2) set block_manager.min_block_size=4KB, 3) set cache.prefix_exclude_regex=(^prompt:hash:).

ashok: do it. do a canary first on a single host in the pool, then scale. watch eviction_ops and 95p latency.

maria: rolling the configs now. command:

```
# canary change
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/runtime-config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"region":"us-west-2","overrides": {"continuous_batch_window_ms": 30, "block_manager.min_block_size": 4096, "cache.prefix_exclude_regex":"^prompt:hash:"}}'
```

maria: canary applied to host i-0a12b34c. monitoring.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for runtime-config/1945679012 on i-0a12b34c. checks: health, eviction_ops, tail_latency.

sofia: within 2 minutes: eviction_ops/sec on canary host down 70%, 95p latency down ~90ms. block_count growth halted.

ashok: good. start region roll after 5 min stable window. also push a small hotpatch to the block manager to add a safety check preventing sub-1KB allocations — low risk.

jamie: hotpatch diff (py):
```
--- a/runtime/block_manager.py
+++ b/runtime/block_manager.py
@@
-    def allocate_block(size):
-        block = allocate_raw(size)
+    def allocate_block(size):
+        # safety: prevent pathological tiny allocations
+        if size < 1024:
+            size = max(size, config.min_block_size)
+        block = allocate_raw(size)
         return block
```

maria: applying hotpatch to canary host and running smoke tests.

deploy-bot: hotpatch deployed to canary; smoke tests passed.

customer-alert-bot: Drafting status update for affected tenants:

"We experienced degraded inference latency in us-west-2 due to a KV cache fragmentation event. A targeted configuration change and hotfix have been rolled out; metrics indicate recovery. We will follow up with a post-incident review."

maria: can we tag the handful of customers who reported errors? customer-alert-bot: please send personalized note once roll complete.

customer-alert-bot: queued messages to 4 customers; will send on final confirmation.

sofia: rolling region-wide now (staggered 10 hosts at a time). monitoring dashboards show evictions returning to baseline across hosts as they pick up the new config.

ashok: after 12 minutes post-roll, global 95p latency back to baseline, error rate normalized. marking immediate incident mitigated.

opsbot: Incident 1945679012: mitigated — continuous-batching induced KV cache fragmentation — mitigation: runtime config roll + block_manager hotpatch.

ashok: good job team. open follow-ups: 1) postmortem to own root cause (why batch window auto-bumped so aggressively), 2) add alert for block_count growth rate, 3) test harness for block allocation scenarios. I'll schedule a PagerDuty handoff/retro.

maria: i'll create the incident doc and include the canary logs + config diffs.

jamie: note: consider longer-term: smarter allocation coalescing in block manager (coalesce adjacent small allocations) and better backpressure on batching heuristics.

sofia: also add a regression test that recreates this fragmentation pattern (we can use traces from the canary).

oncall: handing off to next oncall (ashok -> priya) at 20:00 UTC. priya, assign if you want the postmortem action owner.

priya (not in channel yet): acknowledged — i'll take the postmortem.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup: :tada:

ashok: closing thread once postmortem doc link posted.

maria: postmortem created: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/1945679012-postmortem
